title: TDScore: Learning Synthetic Speech Quality Predictors from TTS Training Dynamics without Human annotation
abstract: Subjective listening tests are the standard for evaluating synthetic speech quality, but they are costly, time-consuming, and difficult to scale. Automatic speech synthetic quality predictors reduce reliance on human ratings, but still depend on large amounts of human-annotated data and generalize poorly across languages, speakers, and synthesis paradigms. This paper proposes a framework without human annotation for learning synthetic speech quality predictors by exploiting training dynamics of text-to-speech systems as pseudo annotation. Synthetic speech is collected from multiple TTS models at different training checkpoints and paired with training-derived metadata such as iteration index and loss. A quality predictor is trained from audio without human perceptual labels. Experiments on benchmark datasets covering multiple languages show that iteration annotation correlates with human annotation across datasets and languages.
relevance_note: Learns synthetic speech quality predictors from TTS training dynamics without human labels; automatic evaluation of synthesized speech.
